messages:
jenna: Quick sync — we're planning to change the default routing fallback semantics when a route's preferred model is OOS. Currently /v1 routes auto-fallback to the nearest compatible model and inherit route-level quotas. Proposal: in v2 the fallback should prefer cost-tiered alternatives and NOT inherit per-route quotas by default. Need thoughts on compatibility surface and console UX for rollouts.

omar: can you paste a short example of current vs proposed behavior? :eyes:

jenna: sure — current behavior (v1):
```http
POST /v1/infer
{
  "route": "widget-summarize",
  "model": "redwood-ggml-16k",
  "input": "..."
}
```
If redwood-ggml-16k is unavailable we auto-fallback to redwood-16k and the request counts against widget-summarize's quota.

Proposed v2: fallback picks a cheaper compatible model (redwood-8k-quant) and charges from a shared fallback pool unless a route explicitly opts-in to inherit quotas.

liam: breaking change for customers expecting quota accounting to stay per-route. We should offer a graceful opt-out (escape hatch) in the console and via header flag, not just API versioning.

jenna: agreed. idea: default to v2 behavior for new tenants and keep a migration window for existing tenants where a compatibility header keeps v1 semantics: `X-RW-Compat: quota-inherit=on`. After 6 months we'll deprecate that header.

sophia: for the Console UX — show a badge on any route that has fallback quota inheritance disabled. Also add a per-route toggle and a small tooltip explaining cost/latency tradeoffs. We should surface an estimate of delta cost when toggling.

omar: technical concern — routing runtime currently resolves models and quotas in one code path. Splitting inheritance will touch the fast path. Need to ensure we don't add contention to the cache keys. Suggest adding a two-step resolution: 1) model candidate selection, 2) quota attribution. Keep model selection lock-free.

liam: agree with two-step. Also logging: we must tag fallback-origin and quota-origin in telemetry. Otherwise billing and alerts will be confusing. Add `fallback_origin` and `quota_origin` fields to traces.

jenna: +1 on telemetry. We'll add a migration telemetry flag `routing_compat_mode` to identify tenants still on v1 semantics. Ops can query it for rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/routing-fallback-v2 -> staging at 2026-04-12T09:30Z :shipit:

omar: small API note — instead of `X-RW-Compat` header maybe we expose `routing.legacy_quota_inherit=true` in the tenant config API so it's visible in console and infra. Headers are ephemeral and hard to audit.

jenna: good point. we'll do tenant-level config + header override for testing. Add migration playbook: 1) enable v2 for new tenants, 2) flag existing tenants, 3) surface tooling to run dry-runs (simulate cost deltas), 4) 90-day notice before disabling header.

liam: can we add a short CLI check to run against a customer's routing table to show potential quota attribution changes? This will help AE and SREs during migration.

jenna: yes — I'll file a ticket for a `rw-inspect routing-compat --tenant <id>` tool.

sophia: UX checklist: tooltip, per-route toggle, cost estimate, migration banner in Console, audit log entry when tenant toggles compatibility.

jenna: thanks — I'll draft the migration doc and follow up with a proposal PR. If no objections, we'll start the staging rollout tomorrow. :thumbsup:
